raw_response:
I have only 4.1 mu, so even though I understand the technical recommendations, I still manage this land like a household farm first, not like a company. Wheat and maize together are the safest for me here in Quzhou. I know this rotation well, the timing fits our land, and with some family members working off-farm I cannot make the system too complicated. For wheat, I will stay close to the local planting window in early October, use a reliable improved variety, and put most of the fertilizer up front with one topdressing at jointing. I do not want to cut fertilizer too much because losing yield on such a small area hurts more than saving a little cash. Since I have well water, I will keep wheat irrigation at the key stages, but not overdo it because pumping costs money. After wheat harvest, I will turn around quickly into summer maize, with simple land preparation and fast planting so I do not lose soil moisture or miss the season. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, apply a moderate nitrogen rate split between planting and jointing, and irrigate only if rainfall is short. My goal is steady yield and stable household income, not chasing the absolute maximum.
